utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor against Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell us, what were you doing on the 15th of April, 1993; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, '93, I went to Vitez to work to the Sutre shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was that a usual day for you, just a normal working day, or was this something special?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was just like all the previous days when I worked in that shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember if you saw any friends of yours that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember there were people who would always come regularly to buy merchandise. There were some, my friends, who came to the retail store. Zdravko Vrebac and Ilija Grabovac are people I remember, and also Veljko Cato, my best man, Krdzalic, Batric, Gavro Mucibabic. I remember them because they were in the shop for some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What were they doing in that shop on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They came to buy some merchandise. Two or three of them had their own coffee shops or restaurants and they were getting their supplies from me, so they just came to collect that merchandise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why is it you remember that those people were in your shop that day? Why do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it has to do with the day that followed, the war in Ahmici, and I was remembering that and then I remembered that 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that Zdravko Vrebac was in your shop that day too, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see him again that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I finished my work, that was until about 5.00 in the afternoon, I usually dropped into that coffee shop because the musicians usually met there. So that evening, they also stopped by, and as I did not have a car, I would go there and then I would find somebody there to give me a lift home. Somebody would always be there in his coffee shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What is this coffee shop called?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was called Set.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you notice there something out of the ordinary, something unusual, showing that the situation was not quite as normal as all that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not notice anything that would be abnormal in the coffee shop. It was all as on all the previous days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When did you go home and who gave you a lift?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could have stayed an hour, an hour and a half there, and it was Zdravko's cousin. Her name was Ivana Vrebac, and it was in her car that I went home. There was another relative with them, so I went to their house and then I walked back to my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where is their house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that shelter that we explained and a little before that shelter, that is, before Zume.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On your way home, as you rode in that car, did you see any movement on the road? Were there more checkpoints than usual?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nothing unusual in comparison with previous days. There was only the checkpoint which was regular at the railway station. It was still there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What happened when you got home?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I got home, my son Marko was ill. He was running a fever. It was a cold. My wife told me that Ivica had arrived from Germany with his wife but that he had gone somewhere. She didn't know where.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was at home. I heard a car arrive, and I assumed it was Ivica, so I went out, saw it was his car. After that, I went to Ivica's, to his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Whom did you find there when you got there? Were there many people or were they just getting in?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I got there, the house was full already. There were Ivica and Ankica. Ivica is my uncle. Ivica's father, Ivo. Nana, that was Ivica's aunt. That's what we called her. Then the refugees, Didaks, Marica and Manda, with their children. Mirko Sakic, Miroslav Pudze. There were many people there already.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What was the conversation about?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember that I talked with Ankica about her residence, about her life in Germany. Then Branko, Avica's middle brother, he had been to Germany for some 15 years, so it must have been some five years that I had not seen him. And then we talked about Josip, who was the last one of them, how he had managed, and young Ivica's brother Ranko was a disabled person, and I enquired after his health. That was roughly what the conversation was about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you talk with Ivica Kupreskic about something particular?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Ivica had been absent for two days, so we talked about the work that I did during those two days, what I had done. I told him that we needed some merchandise in the retail shop, that some of the merchandise should be transferred from the wholesale to the retail shop. And part of our conversation was about usual business.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at Ivica's that evening?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I stayed a little bit longer. My wife was there for a very short time because of little Marko, because he was ill. I wouldn't know what time it was exactly. It could have been 11.00 when I went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That night, did you go to stand guard?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the time, there was no guard duty, so I didn't go out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How long was it that you did not have any guard duty before that and why?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you how long exactly, but Mirko Vidovic had gone to Germany some 15 or 20 days before that, I wouldn't know exactly how long it was, and Ivica was away all the time. I was busy about music and other business. Mirko Sakic, who once was part of that, was busy with RC (phoen), and we simply -- no, we did not discuss it. We simply were not there. We did not go out. We did not replenish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who woke up in the morning? What happened in the morning

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the morning, my brother Zoran woke me up, telling me that an attack from Barin Gaj was expected.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How did you take that? Did it sound serious to you or not? And what did he look like; was he upset, was he agitated?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at the time that he was telling me, he was already fully dressed when he told me that. I never forgot the first conflict and how I went through that and how I got my children out, so I responded to every such news.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Meanwhile, between the first and the second conflict, did you ever react to similar reports?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it happened that we had reports on a couple of occasions, and we would take out our families and spend some time, and after nothing happened, we would go back home.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why do you say that this was an unusual time?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because those previous reports, the previous news, when we would get them, it would usually be before nightfall or immediately after nightfall, and that morning it was different.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did Zoran tell you exactly? Do you remember? Did you ask him something?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did, yes. I asked Zoran where did he get this news, and he said that Anto Vidovic had been to his place and told him so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you inform anyone about what Zoran told you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not inform anyone. I had my mother-in-law, who was also ill, and I could only mention, as an example, that she needed ten minutes to cover 100 metres. She had back pain. She could move with a stick, but with great difficulty. My Marko was ill. When I woke up my wife, she told me that he had barely slept that night because he cried a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It's true you lived in the house with your parents, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The parents were on the ground floor of the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My parents were on the ground floor, and I was on the upper floor of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That upper floor, is there a separate entrance?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there are two independent entrances. We have the same staircase, but the front door where my father and my mother lived was separate, and there was a separate front door to the place where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who informed your parents that an attack was expected and that they should leave the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zoran, after he roused me, he also went to rouse the parents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So why is it that you did not inform anyone? What was the reason for that? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know whom to inform. I had duties towards my families. Zoran told me, "Wake up your family. Get your family and go to the shelter."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: But did you notify Croats who were around you? Did you call Ivica Kupreskic or Vlatko Kupreskic or relatives?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not call them, but Zoran, when we already were on our way, told me that Dragan had roused Ivica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So when your family got ready and when you left, how did you leave and what did you do to prepare for this move to Zume?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, my wife got the children ready. I know that my wife and I were talking about how to bring my mother-in-law, seeing how she was, and we decided to take her in a wheelbarrow. We decided to put her into that wheelbarrow, and it was -- that is what we decided, that she would be in the wheelbarrow and Ivica would carry little Marko, whereas Ankica could walk on her own.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you take any belongings with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My wife had a bag with the children's affairs. It was a rather small bag. Since my mother-in-law was in that wheelbarrow, so I put that bag into that wheelbarrow too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Which route did you take to Zume?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We went through that depression that we used to take before, because it is the shortest way to the centre of Zume and the Croat population.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where were your parents and Zoran and his family then?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I left my house and after we had put my mother-in-law in that wheelbarrow, my father and mother were there, and my father also helped with the mother-in-law, and we left together. Zoran had got there by that time, and we started together, by my uncle's house, towards that depression. We went together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you took that road through the depression; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, through the depression by Niko Sakic's house and on towards Vrebacs' house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see any people next to Niko Sakic's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were people. There were some neighbours living near Niko's house. They were in front of the house, and there were also people who were on the road already moving onward.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Apart from these people, there were your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Apart from these people, did you see anyone else on your way to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the part of the road next to Anto Pudze's house, there was an exit from the road there, and there we saw a group of soldiers. They already were on that road, they were moving, so that when I came up, I walked past them. They were coming in this direction, and we went in the other direction. Some soldiers were also coming off that road next to Anto's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How did the soldiers look?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can say that I only saw these kinds of soldiers on film, and they looked as commandos. I saw white belts, white holsters for pistols. Several of them had their faces painted, and I only saw them in passing. I was driving this wheelbarrow with my children by me. And as I saw them passing by, they also had several cases of ammunition, several of them had them as they were coming in, but all this was just in passing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you ask the soldiers anything? Did you try to talk to them, to ask them where they were going and what was going on?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we said nothing. My mother and father were ahead of me, and Zoran also was ahead of me and he had already passed, and I was among the last with my wife and pushing this wheelbarrow. They had already passed, and they were very quiet and there was no conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did they talk among themselves at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not hear them say a word. They were very quiet. They were even walking very quietly, their footsteps were quiet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How did you know what army this was?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the area where we saw them, there were Croatian houses. Had they been anybody else's houses, something would have happened by then, so it was a Croatian area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Based on how they looked, were you able to determine what unit this was?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The only thing that we could make out was those white belts. So on the basis of that, we concluded that these were the military police, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How about the insignia on the uniforms? Did they have any markings, any insignia?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not make it out. There were some types of insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So then you left your family in Josip Vrebac's shelter?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I left them in Josip Vrebac's shelter, and we went back to Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why did you go back to Niko Sakic's house? Why didn't you stay with your family in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Even before, when we took our families to the shelter, we would always come back, usually to my uncle's barn, and that's where we would spend that day or that part of the day, and this is how we also believed that this day was going to be spent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. So you said that you went back there because you were used to going back to this depression. Why?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not say that we went back into the depression specifically. Earlier, when we would be told to do this, we would come back usually to my uncle's barn, and we would just stay around there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: But what did you think that you would be doing there? What was your thinking at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, we had no idea what we were going to do. Before, we would just come back there and stay around that area, and we believed that on that day we would do the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where were you when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the shooting started, I was with Dragan Vidovic, Mirko Sakic, Dragan Samija, Drago Grgic, and Milutin Vidovic. We were in front of Mirko's shelter. He lived on the top floor, and at the bottom, he has a separate entrance, and from that side, that is where the shelter was, on the back side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see whether Niko Sakic's shelter at that time was full?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did you do when you heard shots?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the shooting started, the bullets were whizzing by. I described -- I don't know how far it was from us, but they were coming this way. So when it started, we ran down into this depression, and we moved up towards that path which led towards our houses, from where we had come earlier that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why did you go over there into this depression near that path?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At first, we just ran down into it in order to take shelter from the shooting, and also, we were close to this path which was the only path leading towards our houses, and so we just stayed there to observe what was going on ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, I'm going to ask you to look at a series of photographs and tell me what you can see there.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D109/2.

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the depression. This is the path leading from Niko Sakic's house down into this depression. This is where we ran, into this part (indicating), and went over to this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These photographs were taken this year in April, that is, in the season similar to the one described by you. Was the vegetation similar to the one in the photograph or was it more green, less green?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that it was a bit more green but close to this. The leaves had started coming out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is the depression as seen from Niko Sakic's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How did you come here? What road did you take?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here, you can see the path. You can see a little bit of growth here (indicating), but this is where we would come down and go to Niko Sakic's house, and then past the house towards the Vrebac shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So that is the path that takes the very edge of the depression?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes we would take that path, and sometimes we would just come down straight into it, but we would avoid it because we didn't want to disturb the grass sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you took the path rather than go through the depression?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and I pushed a wheelbarrow right down this path, right here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the next photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D110/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what can you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This path, this is the part that leads from our houses, if you come down this way (indicating), and this is when you enter the forest from that area. You see here that this path is going towards the path which I pointed out in the previous photographs, where we had come down towards Niko Sakic's house, and here is another path which goes straight through the middle of the forest. When we arrived, when we came running into this depression, we could still see this path and we could see the path leading towards our houses. So it's the only path coming up towards our houses, and then here (indicating), it forks into two or three different paths that lead through the forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you used this lower path down here to go to Niko Sakic's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We came down this way, and then taking this path, we went down to the part of the path which I'd shown you before in order to go down to Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some additional photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D111/2.

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Shall I take the whole batch and then point out the ones that need to be pointed out?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what do you see on the first and second photographs?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This here is the new structure which has been built since I've been here, I don't remember it, and this is what leads down to that path which then takes you down into the depression, and this is from Ivo Kupreskic's house, my uncle's house, down towards that path leading into the depression.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where is Ivo Kupreskic's barn which you referred to?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The barn is right behind this structure here (indicating), about 10 to 15 metres away, and it's also on that slope; in other words, it's lower than this vantage point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please look at photograph number 3 on the next page?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Here, we see exactly what I was referring to a moment ago. This is when we go through the forest, and we were looking at this point before where they fork. This is the path which we took that morning, and the other fork goes through the middle of the forest, and then here is another path which then merges with the one that we had taken down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The path which you did not take and which goes through the middle of the forest, does it also emerge out of the forest at the Niko Sakic's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please look at photograph number 4?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On photograph number 4, you see the same area but a bit closer up. Here, you see the path going into the forest, and then through those trees, you can see the depression down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And photographs 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is now a view taken from the depression itself, so this is the path coming from our houses towards the depression, and here you can see the path very clearly. So this is the path coming down from our houses, and this is the beginning of this clearing, the depression.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: If you can now, please, look at photographs 7 and 8 and describe what you see?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the same area, again, from the depression looking towards the path coming from our houses, and here you see the new structure which at the time did not exist at all. So from this area, the path goes down this way and leads into this depression.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These photographs, D111, were taken a little bit later so you can see that the growth is thicker?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it's greener than in the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you said that you stayed in that part of the depression, in that part of the depression that is closer to your houses; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that part, we could see what was going on on the path that I described to you a few minutes ago, and we could see my uncle's house and this path that led to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where was Zoran at that time when you arrived in the depression?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: While we were in this shelter by Niko's house, by the time we had returned, Zoran had taken Marica and Manda Didak with their children to where his own family was, Mira and his children. When we ran into the depression, Zoran was not with us, this was a matter of a few minutes, but immediately after this shooting, Zoran rejoined us there. He found us at that place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were the people who were with you in the depression armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a rifle which I used during these village guards. I described how I got it. Mirko Sakic had a rifle. As far as I can remember, Dragan Vidovic had a rifle. Drago Grgic and Dragan Samija did not have any weapons, and Zoran, when he joined us, he had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember what these men were wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot remember all the details concerning all the men, but as far as Zoran is concerned, I know that he wore this camouflage jacket. It seems to me that Dragan also wore a camouflage jacket. As for Drago Grgic and the others, I don't think they had any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wore jeans, blue jeans. I wore them to work, so I got back from work wearing them. I had a longish brown jacket. It was warm. Underneath, I had a greenish sweater. I remember that very well because I came in the evening wearing these clothes, and in the morning, I only took the jacket as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you sleep with your clothes on?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not sleep with my clothes on. When I came back from work wearing those clothes, I left those same clothes to be ready for the morning so that I could wear them to work again, and then I went to bed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You're trying to say that you only added the jacket, as compared to what you wore the previous day?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I only added the jacket because it was warm, and I hadn't worn it the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What was the weather like that morning?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was cold.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did it rain?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It didn't rain, but there was a bit of a drizzle, as far as I can remember. I don't know whether it was a drizzle or whether there was simply a mist, but there was something.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend in this depression?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This first terrible shooting lasted two or three hours, I can't say for sure. That was the most terrible part as far as shooting is concerned. We tried a few times to get out along that path that went above so that we could see something, and, I don't know, 15 minutes or 20 minutes later or half an hour later, I cannot tell, a shell fell and it terrified us, and we tried to see something from that part of the path. There is another part of this depression which is in the forest itself and that shell fell into that part which is in the forest. Fortunately, it didn't harm us in any way. We were just terrified, so then we went back. Again after a certain amount of time, we tried to leave, we tried to get out and to see a bit, but this one shell had fallen, the one that terrified us, and in addition to that, there were also bullets that went through that forest, and you could hear the bullets hitting the trees in that forest, and we just tried to get out and we'd have to go back again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: From that position where you were, that is to say, in that part of the depression where you could move, could you see what was going on in the village?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We could not see what was going on in the village but we could see the smoke. There was smoke coming from the direction of our houses, and at those moments when we would try to get to this path, we could see smoke towards the road or somewhere towards the mosque. There was a high pillar of smoke rising from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: At the point in time when you saw that some houses were on fire, did you realise what was going on? Did you manage to draw any conclusions on that basis?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that point in time, we realised there was shooting, terrible shooting. We didn't know what all this was about. At first when we saw this smoke around our houses, I know that Zoran said, "It seems to me that your house is burning," and then afterwards it seemed to him that his house was on fire. We simply thought that all around our houses were on fire. However, at that point in time, we did not realise what was going on and what houses were in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that a shell had fallen into the depression next to the place where you were. Did you hear several shells at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were detonations, especially from that part where we heard small arms fire, but also on the right-hand side, we also heard shells falling.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could you tell where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We could not have known where it was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, while you were in the depression, did anyone come to see you during these first three hours?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When there was a first lull in this shooting, then Milutin Vidovic came, and he said that he was to our left. I don't know exactly who he was with, but he said that he was in that part, and he came to see what was going on and whether we had any information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did he have any information? Did he know more? Could he see more?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Approximately everything that we knew, he knew. That is why he came to see us, to see whether we had any information. Perhaps he even had a better view because he was a bit higher up than we were, so perhaps he saw the smoke better, but he did not have any information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did he tell you exactly where he was?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not know exactly, but he said the part called Bijela Zemlja, that is to say, to the right of our houses, Mira Samija, Mira Vidovic's house, that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Is his house nearby?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly but perhaps 300 or 400 metres away from him. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That is the Milutin Vidovic in whose house some women and children had sought shelter too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you leave that depression?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After this lull, when there was no shooting, because of these shells that we heard coming from the right-hand side, and we thought that this was Zume, that shells were falling on Zume as well, we didn't know how our families were, and we took advantage of that particular moment to go there and see what was happening to our families. So we took the same path where we took our families that morning, we took it in order to reach that same shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did you see as you were passing along that path and going to Zume?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we reached this first shelter by Niko Vidovic's house, Satko Vidovic, Anto Vidovic nicknamed Satko, that is, we called him Satko, he called me and said that this friend of mine, Fahrudin, had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did he tell you? How come he had received this information?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked him at that point, "How did you get this information? Are you sure about this?" And he said that someone from the lower part of Zume had told him, I don't know who this was, and that the information came from Fahrudin's mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So that the information was correct; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that the information was correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did he tell you about the circumstances under which Fahrudin Ahmic had been killed?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He did not describe any circumstances to me. The only conversation we had was that I asked him whether he was sure, although under these circumstances I should not have been suspicious. Anyone could have lost his life.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When you heard about the death of Fahrudin Ahmic, how did you react?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: How could you react when you worked with a person every year for ten days, you played music together for ten days? If it had not been for him, we would not have played on that last Easter. He was the only one who had brought us together to do that. We came together. This was only five days earlier. Zdravko and I and Fahrudin came to play music on that Easter, and this was at this place called Kalvarija. At Kalvarija, that's where the central celebration was supposed to take place. Since it was raining, we carried our instruments up there on foot, and then we were informed that the concert at Kalvarija would not be held and that we had to go back to this cafe. Then we were supposed to take all these instruments and to carry them down and walk on foot, and Zdravko said, "We are not doing this," I said, "We're not doing this." Then this man was the only one, he said, "Come on, let's do it. We played for Bajram, so let's play for Easter, too." It was only because of this man that we actually played music on Easter. When I heard about it that day --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you go and convey this piece of information to someone else?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: By this shelter, I met Zdravko Vrebac, who played music with us on that very same day, and I conveyed that piece of information that I had heard to him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Zdravko Vrebac was also on good terms with Fahrudin; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zdravko played with Fahrudin for as long as I had. The three of us were inseparable friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you went to the shelter to see your wife, did you hear about some details concerning what had happened in Ahmici on that day over there as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some people had some information. It seems to me that when we were going back, Zoran had said that those who were staying with his wife had received information that by this road there were other persons who were killed. Everybody asked. Everybody did not know in detail what had happened. I was there with Zdravko. I told him about what Satko had told me, and Satko told me that because he knew very well how friendly I was with Fahrudin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you hear about any other names on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not hear any other name, but we heard that there were other casualties by the road near Fahran's, that is to say, around the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, after that, did you go back to the depression?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After a certain period of time, I don't know how much time we had spent there with Zdravko and visiting with our families, I went back with Mirko to Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We stayed at Niko Sakic's house briefly, and then we went back to these men who were in the depression and whom we had left there before we departed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did anybody come up then? Did you see any of your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we arrived by Niko Sakic's house, we saw Nikola Omazic, who told us that Mirjan Santic had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This Nikola Omazic, did he wear civilian clothes or a uniform?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Is his house nearby?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Across the street from Niko Sakic, perhaps 100 metres away, that's where his house is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was he on guard duty with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he was never on guard duty with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why, why not?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know why not, but he did not stand guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So he told you about the death of Mirjan Santic?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From him, we received this information that Mirjan Santic had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you know Mirjan Santic?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew him. He was from the neighbourhood where our sister was married, that part of the village, and as of late I had seen him by the railway station as I went to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did he do there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a military policeman. He was in charge of traffic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know who took Mirjan Santic away and where to?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we came to the place where we had been that morning, to this road that leads from our houses, Ivica and this Nikola -- I mean Ivica Kupreskic took Mirjan Santic's body and put it on a ladder. Then the four of us got closer to them, and then we altogether carried the body to Niko Sakic's garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That Mirjan Santic, was his face painted?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, his face was not painted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember if he had any insignia on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mirjan Santic's body, he had a camouflage uniform, HVO military police insignia on his shoulder, and I remember a ribbon of sky blue, very light blue, more white than blue ribbon, something of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you carried the body to Niko Sakic's garage. Do you know who carried Mirjan Santic and where after that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not hear if his father or some relatives came and took it away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: His house is in Santici, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: His house is in Santici, in the second part, not where Zume-Santici is but a bit farther away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That group of soldiers that came up that road which you saw when you went to the shelter, did you notice Mirjan Santic in that group?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On that 16th of April, did the gunfire abate at some point or stop?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. When we heard UNPROFOR APCs and could see them, because that is where we were on this path, at that moment there was complete silence, there was no gunfire at all. Those two APCs went by the warehouse in the direction of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see them or only hear them?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were on that part of the path, and we could also see them through the forest as they drove past. Of course, the sound reaches you first, and by that sound -- when hearing that sound, we went out to see, and then when we came up, we saw that they were moving in the direction of Upper Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: After that, was there any gunfire after those APCs left Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Immediately after they left, the gunfire started again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That day, at any time, could you say that the gunfire had stopped completely, that no sound came? I mean sound of gunfire or fighting or operation. Could you tell us if there was that kind of silence on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only in that part, that first time which we used to go to our families, there was no gunfire. And when those APCs were there, for as long as they were there, there was no gunfire. Then perhaps in the afternoon, it could have been around 4.00 or 5.00, I would not know, there was another lull. After that, the gunfire resumed again, and it finally stopped only after nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What parts of Ahmici did this gunfire come from?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In front of us from where we were, in front of us, in all of the parts. In all the parts in front of us. I don't know exactly. That is, to the side, as I have said, to the right side, that is the main road, and from those sides, there was also gunfire there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could you hear any gunfire around your houses in the afternoon or was it getting further away? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot describe it with any accuracy. Perhaps it felt less around our houses than in the morning. But as that day progressed and towards the evening, the most intensive gunfire could be heard from around the mosque and that part towards the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that the gunfire stopped in the evening of the 16th of April. Would you know where the Croat units were positioned at the moment when the gunfire stopped? Could you judge their positions? Where were their positions, roughly? Could you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not really judge their positions when the gunfire stopped. When we came out, walking to that stable, which I already explained where we were, one could hear people calling. There was a word, and I was trying -- or many times I tried very hard to remember that word because it rang in my ears, but I cannot remember that word which was used. I understood that it was that particular word which they used to communicate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where did you hear those calls, those --

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it's the night, and the echo is much more intensive at night. But it was over our houses and then on towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Above your houses?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In front and above, towards Ahmici; that is, not in our direction but behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where did you spend that night between the 16th and the 17th?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We spent that night -- when I was showing to you that new structure, in front of it is that path, and there was a small gully where we spent the night. Well, some spent it in the stable, and some of us spent it in that gully.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What were you doing there? Did you still watch that nobody would come close to the shelter, or did you sleep, or what?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, come, what's sleep? Nobody felt like sleeping. Nobody slept a wink that night. We were there because we were outside the woods and in front of us was a clearing, so we could see if anyone came in our direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, was the gunfire resumed in the village?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the morning, as soon as the day broke, the gunfire started again. But in the morning, it was at some distance and it was moving towards the upper parts of Ahmici. That is, one did not hear it anymore around the mosque or our houses. We simply could hear it move away towards the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In the lower part of Ahmici, could you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we could not hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did you think at that time had happened to the local Muslims? You only heard the gunfire moving towards Upper Ahmici. What about the Muslims from the lower part of the village, from those around your houses below the road?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The information we heard or received on that 16th, what Ivica told me, that all those houses were on fire, all those houses belonging to neighbours around our houses. What we saw during the night, that the mosque had been destroyed, that all those houses and all that up there was on fire. Those two or three times we went to see our families towards Zume, we could also see the houses set on fire and burning down, and of course at that moment we could realise, indeed, that Muslims had perished there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: But there was also fire directed at Gornji Ahmici, and on the basis of that gunfire, what could you infer? Was fighting going on there or were civilians being under attack? What was it that you inferred?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not infer anything about the fighting. I didn't know who was involved in fighting. But some of the houses which I described and which I mentioned had burnt down, and we realised that they belonged to Muslims. As for the people, we didn't know at the time. We did not think that there were all that many victims, that people had managed to pull out, to find some shelter, but we did not know at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, apart from that gunfire that you heard in the direction of Gornji Ahmici, did anything else happen that day that would stick in your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the evening of the 17th, after the nightfall, Mirko Sakic told us that all the people from the shelter where my family had been, that they all had escaped over to Rovna, and from the shelter in Niko Sakic's house, they had also escaped, because his family had been in that shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why did they escape?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because a report had arrived allegedly that from Krtina-Mahala, that part of the line had been broken through, and people were afraid and they all fled.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did this report say that Muslims were coming?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that it was reported that the line had been broken through, that the Mujahedin had broken through the line on the Krtina -- at the Krtina-Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you know what was going on with your family?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. At that moment, I didn't know anything about them, and then I went to the shelter to see whether they were there and what was happening to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Whom did you find there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I went there together with Zoran, and we found Zoran's wife there. She told me that my people had gone towards Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you go to Rovna to see your family, to see where your wife and your two children were and her mother?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't go there then because it was dark, so I did not go to Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When did you go to Rovna?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the morning, as soon as it dawned, I went to Rovna and I found my family in Pero Santic's house. The parents were there and my wife and my mother-in-law, and I found them safe and sound there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was it that you went to Rovna; early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As soon as that day broke is when I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: After that, when you saw that your family was safe, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I went back again to my brother's and those other neighbour's, where they were all at Niko's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why did you go back there? Why did you go back if your family was safe?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, my brother was there. I went to see my brother and those other people with whom I had been.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were there any other Croat women in Zume and around those shelters? Would you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When this information reached us from Krtina-Mahala, from Krtina-Mahala, the majority of women and children came down to the shelter where my family had been, their shelter. So they simply took their place. These people went to Rovna and those others took over that shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When did you go to your house for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I returned from Rovna, in that part near Niko's house, Zdravko Vrebac came in his car to see us, and then it occurred to me, as there was this car and as Zdravko was there, to try to salvage my accordion from the house. He could take it back to his house and keep it there. So I left with Zdravko and went to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So even then you didn't go because of the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it just happened that Zdravko was there with his car. It was Zdravko, and that was why it occurred to me that perhaps I might get my accordion out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why was that accordion so important to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I described the period until 1992. The joy that I had and my only means of livelihood was that instrument, and at that moment, I didn't know whether I would go on living or where I would go to live, but wherever I settled, that again would be the only means of livelihood for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did your house look like when you got there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was chaos. All the things had been pulled out of the drawers, cupboards. Everything was on the floor. All the chest drawers had been pulled out and broken, doors broken. In the nursery, we haven't put window panes again. We can go there and see it. All the window panes were down. There were bullet marks all around the walls. A fire was beginning to burn. Fortunately, it just died out, but I wish sometimes to God that the house had burned down. Perhaps other things wouldn't have happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you notice that anything was missing? You saw all those belongings, all your valuables. Were they still there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, some golden objects, I could not really see at that time, but there were several things missing. A leather jacket was missing. Some of my wife's clothes were missing. I don't really know. Well, yes, it was ransacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Around your house, did you see any marks of bullets, anything that would indicate that your house was under fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In front of the house, one could find very many cartridges, very many shells, right in front of the house as you walk to the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said there were very many empty shells. Did you see anything else, apart from those empty bullet shells? Do you remember anything else?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember, no, not around the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was the door to your house open or shut when you came?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The door was ripped out. It was a wooden door, and the plank, that part of the board with a lock and a handle, was ripped out, ripped off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: After that, you went back to the depression, and who did you give your accordion to?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I got there with Zdravko. I gave it to Zdravko and Zdravko took it away, and the accordion was at his place throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So at that moment, you didn't even know if you would ever live in your house again?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The last thing I thought at the time was that I would ever go back to live there again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What else happened on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 18th, in the afternoon hours, we were by my uncle's stable, in that part, and four or five military policemen came along, I don't know how many of them, and they were taking along a group of people from Vitez, civilians. I knew some of them, and among them was Miro Vujinovic, my best man, the best man at my wedding. They were taking them, and they came across us and they told us that we had to go to Pirici, that defence lines were being formed there, that one had to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In addition to the civilians, how many other people were there, those soldiers who came to get you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, four or five.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In which direction did they take you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We went past Ivica's brother, Branko's house and then past Enver Sehic's house, in other words, through the clearing near his house in the direction of Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did you see on your way?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was only then that we could see how terrible it was, what happened there. There was a body. I was towards the middle of this column, and I saw this body, and I thought that it was this neighbour, Enver Sehic, whose body it was. Then further on on the road, you could see another two bodies. When we came up to Pirici, then from there, you could see what was lying down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did you see from there?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was ghost-like. Everything had been burned. It was terrible. It's very hard for me to describe it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These soldiers, were these soldiers or some military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those were military policemen who had taken us there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we came up there, they split us into groups of two or three, every 40 or 50 metres, and they said that a front line was to be established there, that we needed to dig trenches and that we would spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was anybody there when you arrived in this location?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were other civilians there whom we found there when we arrived who had started digging. There was another group of military policemen. They were dressed similarly to the ones who had brought us there. I also saw several wearing black uniforms. I saw two or three wearing some kind of bandannas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So they ordered you to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In groups of two or three, they assigned us each to one of these groups, and that's where we dug and spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were there any other trenches which the Croats dug before in Ahmici, around your houses or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never saw any trenches dug in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Pirici?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stayed a couple of days, and then I was transferred to the area above Upper Ahmici, and that's where I stayed until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Above Upper Ahmici, you also had trenches?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again it was the same. We came to a clearing, and then we started digging trenches, and then eventually, some kind of a fortified line was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that trench in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stayed there until the end of the war when I was demobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When were you demobilised?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I resumed work sometime in April when the work started again, and I got the document right at the end of the hostilities in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it is convenient, we can take a break now, and then after the break, I have several documents, and we will finish within half an hour after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Let's take our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Kupreskic, I will now show you some documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Please, can the usher assist us in this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D112/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Kupreskic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What is it about?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is my demobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In other words, this is a certificate of your demobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Of 1 June, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it's 31 May, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, but issued on 1 June, 1994. Can you tell me, was this document delivered to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was it delivered?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know if it was delivered on that same day but in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you stop being a soldier, based on this certificate of demobilisation? Was that the time when you ceased carrying out your military duty?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the Sutre company started working again in April, I left that line and turned in everything that had been issued to me, and then later I received this document on demobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you were demobilised at your own request?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can the usher now please show the witness the document, Prosecution Exhibit 353?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please turn to page 30, item 217. Is your first and last name entered under 217?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The date of engagement in the unit, it is until 22 January '96. Is that date correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When were you demobilised?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the document, on 31 May, but I said that I had left the front line in April '94.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether the signature on that line was your signature?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not sign it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Why did you not sign this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nobody called me in to have me sign it, and had they done so, I would have signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know who signed it on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know with what purpose this list was compiled?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was done because of some shares.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask the usher for assistance with another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D113/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Kupreskic, have you ever seen these certificates?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These are certificates on additional pay to members of the armed forces. This first certificate in front of you, is that certificate issued to Zoran Kupreskic, and is it stated there correct, the information in the father's name and the registration number?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What number of months has been accorded to Zoran Kupreskic for additional pay?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The number here stated is "52".

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please turn the page over to certificate number 2. This is a certificate issued to Mira Kupreskic, daughter of Franjo. Do you know who this is?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is Zoran's wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many months was she accorded for additional pay?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The third person is Milka Sakic, daughter of Ivo?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is Ivo Sakic's mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: She was born in 1933, according to the data. Do you see how many months were accorded to her?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The following certificate is Luca, daughter of Mata. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is my mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was she born?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many months were accorded to her for additional pay?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the next certificate issued to Katica Vidovic, daughter of Mija? Do you know who this is?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that this is Mirko Vidovic's spouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: At that time, she was not even in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This woman spent the entire war period in Germany and came back home in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many shares was she accorded, what equivalent?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The equivalent of 45 months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The following certificate is Anto Kupreskic, son of Ante. Who is this person?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was born in 1936. That is my late father.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many shares was he accorded?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When did he die?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He died on 2nd October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Next is Milka Vidovic, daughter of Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is Mirko Vidovic's mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: She was born in 1927?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many shares did she get?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five months' worth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Now Luca Rajic-Miskovic, daughter of Ante, born in 1940?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is Ivo's aunt whom we've been mentioning all along.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this is Ivo Kupreskic's aunt who lived in the old Kupreskic house?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Ivo Kupreskic, son of Ante, born in '25, who is this person?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is my uncle, Ivica's father.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many shares did he get?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five months' worth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: There are additional certificates here, but let me take you to Mirjan Kupreskic, son of Ante, born in '63. Is this you?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many shares were you allotted?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-nine months' worth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Then Ljubica Kupreskic, daughter of Ivo, born in '66, who is this person?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is my wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many months was she accorded for additional pay?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty-five.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: During the war, you were in trenches, and you said that before the war, you were part of the village guards?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What did Mira Kupreskic do, your wife, Vidovic's mother, what did these women do?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They worked at home, like they always did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were they involved in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In no way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I mean during the war period.

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they were never actively engaged in the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Kupreskic, could you please tell the Court what your relations were like with Sakib Ahmic and his family? I'm referring to his sons.

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My relationship with Sakib Ahmic was the same as with all other neighbours who belonged to that generation. Whenever we would see one another, we would greet each other cordially. As for his sons, I was on the best terms with Naser because we're almost the same age and we went to school together for eight years, and also the younger one, Ezo, I think his name is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were you friends with Naser after you stopped going to school with him?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Naser had a shoemaker shop at the railway station, so when I worked at the wholesale outlet, when he would stop working, he would stop by to see me, have a drink with me or perhaps buy something that he needed. That is the kind of socialising we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see each other in the village too, not only in this shoemaker's shop of his?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not say that we would see each other at this shoemaker's shop. I said that at the railway station, he had this shoemaker's shop, and then when he would finish work, on his way home and as he would pass by the warehouse, he would stop by to see me at the warehouse. He would either buy things that he needed for his home or he would stop by for a drink.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What were your relations like with Sukrija Ahmic? Did you socialise with him?

utterances.speaker: MIRJAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sukrija is considerably older than I am, so just like with Sakib, we would say hello to one another but we were not very close or anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, may we move into private session now just for a few minutes, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.
